title: ReactNative: Migrate ondevice addons from `addons`
body:
Closes https://github.com/storybookjs/react-native/issues/873

## What I did

On-device addons listed in `addons` cause `extract` (story indexing / manifest generation) to fail in `@storybook/react-native` projects because Storybook Core attempts to evaluate them as presets in a Node.js context. The on-device addons contain React Native code that cannot be loaded server-side, resulting in a `CriticalPresetLoadError`.

The fix moves on-device addons to a separate `deviceAddons` field that is only consumed at runtime (by `scripts/generate.js`), not by Core.

### Changes

- **New automigration** (`rn-ondevice-addons-to-device-addons`) — detects `@storybook/react-native` projects and moves any addon whose name contains `"ondevice"` from `addons` → `deviceAddons`; preserves both string and object (`{ name, options }`) forms
- **Registered** in `allFixes` immediately after `rnstorybookConfig`
- **9 tests** covering: guard conditions (no RN, no ondevice addons), string/object addon detection, deps vs devDeps, and run-phase behavior (removal, object preservation, dryRun passthrough)
- **MIGRATION.md** — added `React Native: on-device addons moved to deviceAddons` section (with TOC entry and before/after example) in the 9.x → 10.0.0 chapter

Note: `deviceAddons` is intentionally not added to the shared `StorybookConfigRaw` core type since it is React Native-specific. The automigration uses `ConfigFile`'s string-path APIs to write the field without requiring a type declaration.

**Before / After:**

```ts
// Before (.rnstorybook/main.ts)
export default {
  addons: [
    '@storybook/addon-ondevice-controls',
    '@storybook/addon-ondevice-actions',
    '@storybook/addon-docs',
  ],
};

// After (automigrated)
export default {
  addons: ['@storybook/addon-docs'],
  deviceAddons: [
    '@storybook/addon-ondevice-controls',
    '@storybook/addon-ondevice-actions',
  ],
};
```

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [ ] stories
- [x] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

1. Clone https://github.com/chromaui/pets-in-pajamas (repro repo)
2. With on-device addons in `.rnstorybook/main.ts > addons`, confirm extract fails
3. Run the automigration — confirm addons are moved to `deviceAddons`
4. Confirm extract now succeeds

### Documentation

- [x] Add or update documentation reflecting your changes
- [x] If you are deprecating/removing a feature, make sure to update
      [MIGRATION.MD](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/MIGRATION.md)

comments.body: Casting `status.value as TestStatusValue` can cause a runtime crash if `status.value` is not one of the five allowed keys (e.g., if additional `StatusValue` variants exist for other status systems). In that case `statusValueToStoryIdsMap[status.value]` is `undefined`, and `.push(...)` will throw. Fix by guarding before pushing (e.g., check key existence), or by widening the map to include all possible `StatusValue` keys that can appear for these status types.

<details>
<summary>💡 Suggested hardening</summary>

```diff
-    statusValueToStoryIdsMap[status.value as TestStatusValue].push(status.storyId);
+    const bucket = statusValueToStoryIdsMap[status.value as TestStatusValue];
+    if (bucket) {
+      bucket.push(status.storyId);
+    }
```
</details>

```suggestion
    if (bucket) {
      bucket.push(status.storyId);
    }
```

<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/addons/vitest/src/use-test-provider-state.ts` at line 51, The code
unguardedly indexes statusValueToStoryIdsMap with status.value as
TestStatusValue which can throw if status.value is unexpected; before pushing
status.storyId, add a runtime guard that checks whether status.value is a valid
key (e.g., typeof status.value === 'string' and status.value in

Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(statusValueToStoryIdsMap, status.value))
and only then call statusValueToStoryIdsMap[status.value].push(status.storyId);
otherwise handle the unknown status safely (e.g., ignore, log, or add to a
```

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`For the Vite version range currently used by Storybook builder-vite in this repository, is the following plugin hook shape officially supported?

resolveId: {
  filter: { id: /\/vite-inject-mocker-entry\.js/ },
  handler(source) { ... }
}

Please provide official Vite docs/changelog references that explicitly cover object-form resolveId hooks with filter support.`

💡 Result:

### Vite range used by Storybook `@storybook/builder-vite`
In current Storybook `@storybook/builder-vite` releases, the published peer dependency range for Vite is:

- `vite: "^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0"` ([app.unpkg.com](https://app.unpkg.com/%40storybook/builder-vite%4010.1.1/files/package.json?utm_source=openai))

### Is this object-form `resolveId` hook with `filter` officially supported in that range?
Your hook shape:

```js
resolveId: {
  filter: { id: /\/vite-inject-mocker-entry\.js/ },
  handler(source) { /* ... */ }
}
```

is **officially supported by Vite only starting in Vite 6.3.0+** (and not in Vite 5.x, and not in Vite 6.0–6.2.x), per Vite’s own docs:

- Vite docs show `resolveId: { filter: { id: ... }, handler() { ... } }` as the supported shape. ([vite.dev](https://vite.dev/guide/api-plugin.html))  
- Vite docs explicitly state that “Hook Filters” (the `filter`+`handler` object form for hooks like `resolveId`) are supported in **Vite 6.3.0+** (and Rollup 4.38.0+). ([vite.dev](https://vite.dev/guide/api-plugin.html))

So, **within Storybook’s allowed Vite peer range (`^5 || ^6 || ^7`) this hook shape is only “officially supported” for the subset `vite >= 6.3.0` (and in Vite 7.x), but not for Vite 5.x.**

### Official references explicitly covering “object-form hooks with filter support”
- **Vite Plugin API docs** (example using object-form `resolveId` with `filter` + `handler`). ([vite.dev](https://vite.dev/guide/api-plugin.html))  
- **Vite Plugin API docs → “Hook Filters” section** (states support is **Vite 6.3.0+**). ([vite.dev](https://vite.dev/guide/api-plugin.html))  
- **Rolldown “Plugin Hook Filters” docs** (cross-reference stating hook filters are supported in **Vite 6.3.0+** and describing `resolveId` filter semantics). ([rolldown.rs](https://rolldown.rs/apis/plugin-api/hook-filters?utm_source=openai))

Citations:

- 1: https://app.unpkg.com/%40storybook/builder-vite%4010.1.1/files/package.json?utm_source=openai
- 2: https://vite.dev/guide/api-plugin.html
